question: Can a small shared readout of full frozen token vectors improve natural positive/negative discrimination for unseen source/confusion components?
scope: Historical three-fold cross-fit on 1860 fixed pairs / 1117 photos, not a fresh blind test and not full-gallery retrieval.
features: Original cached valid 128-dimensional tokens only, including valid template tokens; no OCR, coordinates, positions, IDs, order, ROI or edited pixels enter readout.
architecture: Shared bias-free Linear(128,16), tanh, L2 normalization; directional mean MaxSim; residual baseline + beta * learned score.
loss: pair logistic softplus(-target*(baseline_margin + .2*learned_margin)/.03), equal pair weight
selection: Best validation positive-component macro accuracy, averaging pairs within photo first; epoch0..4 and beta in [0,.05,.1,.2,.5,1]. Ties prefer beta0, then smaller beta, then earlier epoch. Separate head-only selection on same validation metric.
labels: True positive-versus-negative. Null controls flip signs for exactly half of training positive components, deterministically per seed/fold; all rows in a component share a flip. Validation and test labels stay true for both pipelines.
splits: Union SHA duplicates, DailyMed set, source group, positive equivalents, human confusion edges and all focal39 confusions. Train/validation/test candidate components are disjoint, including negatives. Grouping is conservative but not an exhaustive independent brand audit.
limitations: Positive references are historical ledger choices; positive equivalence preserved. Hard negatives were mined in earlier full-gallery analyses.
Selection of focal39 and grouping use previously observed historical errors; no claim of untouched test.
Full token cache is frozen; no claim that failure of this 2048-parameter readout proves absence of information.
Color, text, layout, background and templates remain mixed in token vectors; improvement would not isolate layout information.
